chapter: Early life and the New Orleans band scene
title: Colored bands, bandwagons and dance pay in old New Orleans
summary: He recalls the Imperial, Superior, Olympia and Tuxedo bands advertising dances from furniture wagons, Jack Laine's Reliance bands, and pay of a dollar and a half a man.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I remember the colored bands they had all around the city of New Orleans. The Imperial Band. The Superior Band. The Olympia. The Night Millennial. The Tuxedo Band. All the colored bands. They go around. In the days when they'd give a dance, they would sing this band that would play for the dance. They'd go around on a truck. Call it a furniture wagon. Old time furniture wagon. Remember why I see people? How they moved furniture in the old days? Yeah, it was a bandwagon. Yeah. And they put sides on there, you know? With a sign. Where the dance would be. The white bands used to do the same thing. Jack Lane used to have three bands. Called Reliance Band. Number one, number two, and number three. That's why all that stuff was originated. See? From the Negroes. And you take most of the time, these colored bands, you'd get a band with eight men, seven to eight men, for a dime and a half per night. Play five hours. That was, you know, you know.
That was a dollar man had for the whole band.
A man. A man. A man. Oh yeah. That leader would get three dollars. That was big money.
